title: Redis Caching
summary: Redis is an in-memory data store used for caching, supporting key-value storage, TTL expiration, and pub/sub messaging.

content.overview: Redis is an in-memory data store that provides high-performance caching through key-value storage, automatic key expiration, and publish-subscribe messaging.
content.details: Redis supports key-value storage, TTL (time to live) expiration for cache entries, and pub/sub messaging. Common caching use cases include session storage and API response caching, leveraging its speed and data structure flexibility.
content.caveats: Being in-memory, data may be lost on restart unless persistence is configured. TTLs must be managed carefully to avoid stale data or premature eviction.
